paragraphs.text: Silundi , or the Silundi Sea , is the vast stretch of coastal waters that surround the islands of Ondu on the plane of Zendikar . Its channels and bays connect Ondu’s three major islands— Agadeem , Beyeen , and Jwar Isle — to the mainland and each other.
The Bay of Beyeen is the wide channel separating Agadeem and Beyeen . It serves as a major passage for traders and explorers navigating between the two islands and the mainland.
Agadeem - Ondu’s largest island. It is best known for its hedron fields and cryptic tombs:
Fields of Agadeem — open plains scattered with ancient hedron ruins that distort natural laws. Visitors report strange visions, such as drifting masks.

Crypt of Agadeem — an elaborate underground tomb containing the sealed Cryptlock . The crypt is from the Eldrazi era, meaning it is from around -1400 AR . Crypt Maw — a vast bat-infested cavern that marks the tomb’s haunted entrance. Cryptlock — the innermost sealed chamber, binding thousands of dead within its walls.
Kabira — once a kor hunting plateau and crossroads settlement near the hedron fields. It was destroyed by Ulamog ’s brood.
Beyeen is a medium-sized island that sits between Agadeem and Jwar Isle. It is volcanic and geothermally active, with vibrant rainforests nestled among its lava flows.

Crown of Talib — a range of floating volcanic peaks named for Talib , the kor god of the earth. Boilbasin — superheated tide pools formed where seawater meets volcanic springs. Dragons are known to bathe here to cleanse their scales. Mount Valakut — the Crown’s largest and most volatile volcano.
Zulaport — a busy coastal trade port populated by mages, explorers, and artisans of many races. Zulaport was once controlled by the vampire Indorel .
The Serpent’s Maw is the storm-lashed sea that isolates Jwar Isle from the rest of Ondu.
Jwar Isle - known as the Isle of Secrets, the smallest and most remote of Ondu’s major islands. Shrouded in storms and myth, it holds many hidden wonders:
Jwari Faduun — massive pre- Eldrazi stone heads scattered across the isle, where pilgrims bury their dead in reverence.
The Jwari Ruins - half-submerged ruins riddled with pitfalls and traps, left behind when the skyclave rose into the sky.
The Ondu Skyclave — an ancient kor ruin containing ancient labs, lethal traps, and the former lair of Grakmaw .
Strand of Jwar — a pure blue strand of aether that glows and beams skyward from a saltwater pool.
